faq.title: Questions, answered.
faq.q1: How is the Startuper.io programme different from an accelerator?
faq.a1: Accelerators take equity and run fixed curricula. We work on a cohort fee basis and adapt the method to your specific stage, product, and market. We don't batch you through generic workshops — we embed.
faq.q2: What is the time commitment per week?
faq.a2: Expect 4-6 hours of structured sessions per week (strategy reviews, execution sprints, investor prep) on top of your regular building work. The pace is intense by design — momentum compounds when you stay in the loop.
faq.q3: How do you select which startups to work with?
faq.a3: We look for three signals: a live problem with early validation (prototype, pre-revenue or revenue), a committed founding team, and a willingness to be accountable to a weekly rhythm. We turn down most applications because the fit has to be real on both sides.
faq.a4: Absolutely. We sign NDAs upfront. Your metrics, your deck, your strategy — nothing leaves the cohort without your explicit consent.
faq.q5: What happens after the programme ends?
faq.a5: Alumni get lifetime access to our founder network, preferential investor intros, and a reduced rate for follow-on diagnostics.
faq.q6: How does the application process work?
faq.a6: You fill out a short application form describing your startup and your current stage. A partner reviews it personally within 48 hours. If there's a potential fit, we schedule a no-obligation diagnostic call to explore further.
faq.q7: What is the typical programme duration?
faq.a7: The core programme runs for 12 weeks. Some startups extend certain phases depending on their traction velocity and fundraise timeline. We adapt to what the startup actually needs.
faq.q8: How much does the programme cost?
faq.a8: Our pricing is cohort-based and depends on the scope of support. We do not publish standard rates because every engagement is scoped individually. We take no equity — ever. Contact us for a custom proposal.
faq.q9: Can I apply as a solo founder?
faq.a9: Yes. We work with solo founders — but we assess readiness on a case-by-case basis. Solo founders need strong self-discipline and the ability to execute across multiple tracks. We may suggest bringing in a co-founder or key hire before starting.
faq.q10: Do you work with non-tech startups?
faq.a10: Yes. Our method is sector-agnostic. What matters is the existence of a live problem with early validation and a team committed to structured execution. We've worked with SaaS, hardware, marketplace, and service-based startups.

methodPage.title: A method, not a playbook.
methodPage.subtitle: Three structured phases that turn early-stage uncertainty into a raise-ready trajectory. Each phase has concrete deliverables, a clear duration, and a measurable outcome.
methodPage.step1.detail: We start by mapping your entire current state. This is not a surface-level audit — we interview your team, review your product analytics, dissect your unit economics, and identify exactly where momentum is leaking. At the end of this phase, you have a single prioritised roadmap with clear ownership for each item. No more wondering what to work on next.
methodPage.step1.deliverable: Prioritised execution roadmap, product-market fit gap analysis, runway assessment
methodPage.step2.detail: This is where the method compounds. Every week follows a structured loop: customer discovery → hypothesis test → build → measure → review. We run real sessions with real users, not slide decks. You ship something every week. By week 8, your unit economics are visible, your MVP has iterated at least 4 times, and you have a traction curve to show investors.
methodPage.step2.deliverable: Shipped MVP iterations, customer interview transcripts, unit economics dashboard, traction metrics
methodPage.step3.detail: When the metrics speak, we help you tell the story. We build your data room from your actual traction data, craft a pitch deck that matches your stage, map the investors who actually invest in your space, and run dry sessions until the narrative is seamless. You walk into meetings with pattern-matched investors who already understand your space.
methodPage.step3.deliverable: Investor-ready data room, pitch deck, investor target list, dry-run sessions
methodPage.example1.title: From pre-revenue to seed-ready in 10 weeks
methodPage.example1.body: A B2B SaaS startup joined the programme with a prototype and 3 pilot users. Phase 1 revealed they were solving a problem users would pay for — but their pricing model was wrong. Phase 2 shifted focus to value-based pricing and ran 22 customer discovery calls. By week 10, they had 8 paying customers, a clear CAC-to-LTV ratio, and a seed round oversubscribed by 40%. The method didn't create the traction — it eliminated the noise so the traction could surface.
customersPage.title: Founders who ran the method.
customersPage.subtitle: Real results from real founders. No stock photography, no curated quotes — just honest accounts of what changed.
customersPage.case1.title: From solo prototype to paying customers in 8 weeks
customersPage.case1.context: Marie had been building her FinTech prototype alone for 14 months. She had a working MVP, positive feedback from friends, and zero revenue. She was running out of savings and considering going back to full-time employment.
customersPage.case1.problem: The product solved a real problem — freelancers struggling with cross-border invoicing — but Marie had no systematic way to find early adopters. She was building features nobody asked for while neglecting the distribution channel that would actually work.
customersPage.case1.solution: The diagnostic phase mapped her feature backlog against customer demand. We cut 60% of planned features, identified a single distribution channel (niche freelance communities on Slack), and ran weekly customer discovery sprints. Marie talked to 5 freelancers every week for 6 weeks.
customersPage.case1.result: 8 weeks in, Marie had 12 paying customers, a clear ICP, and a waitlist of 40 users. She raised a pre-seed round from a micro-fund that specialises in FinTech. She now runs the product with a team of 3.
customersPage.case2.title: From stuck marketplace to traction in 12 weeks
customersPage.case2.context: Alex and Jordan had been running a two-sided marketplace for local services for 18 months. They had supply (service providers) but struggled to activate demand (customers). Churn was high on both sides.
customersPage.case2.problem: They were spending 80% of their time recruiting more providers while ignoring why customers weren't coming back. The core issue was not the number of providers — it was the booking experience, which took 4 clicks too many on mobile.
customersPage.case2.solution: Week 1–2: we audited the funnel and found the dropout point. Week 3–8: we redesigned the mobile booking flow to 3 taps and ran a demand-side experiment with targeted social ads in one neighbourhood. Week 9–12: we measured retention improvement and prepared the data room.
customersPage.case2.result: Repeat booking rate went from 18% to 41%. Monthly active customers grew 3.2×. The streamlined funnel became the centrepiece of their seed round pitch, which closed at 1.2M.
customersPage.case3.title: Pivot to product-market fit within one cohort
customersPage.case3.context: Tom's team had built an AI-powered analytics dashboard for SMBs. After 6 months of development and 50 beta users, engagement was flat. The team was debating whether to pivot or shut down.
customersPage.case3.problem: The dashboard was a solution in search of a problem. It did many things adequately but nothing urgently. Beta users logged in once and never returned. The team was building features based on what they thought was cool — not on what users needed.
customersPage.case3.solution: We ran a structured reset: 30 customer interviews in 2 weeks to find the real pain point. The insight: SMB owners didn't want more data — they wanted fewer decisions. We pivoted the product to an automated recommendation engine that told them exactly one action to take each day.
customersPage.case3.result: Daily active usage went from 8% to 63%. The new product, Retool, closed 5 paying customers within 3 weeks of launch and was accepted into a top-tier accelerator. The team credits the structured reset for saving 12 months of building in the wrong direction.

aboutPage.title: Built by founders, for founders.
aboutPage.subtitle: Startuper.io exists because the gap between 'building' and 'raise-ready' is wider than most founders expect — and most resources in the market won't help you cross it.
aboutPage.mission: Our mission is simple: eliminate the structural friction that kills early-stage startups. We embed directly into your founding team and run a repeatable method that compresses months of trial-and-error into weeks of structured execution.
aboutPage.vision: We believe every great startup deserves a clear trajectory — not a generic playbook. The admission-by-application model is not about exclusivity for its own sake. It's about ensuring that every founder we work with is ready to commit to the method, and that every partner hour goes to startups that can actually benefit from it.
aboutPage.bio: Sergeo founded Startuper.io after spending a decade building, scaling, and advising early-stage tech companies. He saw the same pattern repeatedly: talented founders with real insights wasting months on process noise instead of traction. The method is his answer — a structured alternative to the chaos of building alone.

privacyPage.section3.title: 3. Cookies
privacyPage.section3.body: We use essential cookies for site functionality and optional analytics cookies to understand how visitors interact with our site. You can manage cookie preferences through your browser settings. We do not use tracking cookies for advertising.
privacyPage.section4.title: 4. Your Rights

privacyPage.section5.body: If you have questions about this privacy policy or our data practices, email us at privacy@startuper.io or write to Startuper.io, 128 Rue de la République, 75011 Paris, France.
